Question 2

Which attribute of INPUT tag defines the number of characters that can be displayed in a text box without scrolling?

  • A. SIZE
  • B. MAXLENGTH
  • C. VALUE
  • D. TYPE

Source

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 18

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate the control role, displayed content, submitted value and form destination.

Study-guide sections

WEB09 · Form controls and successful submission

WEB-S02 · Form values and result destinations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB09 · Form controls and successful submission

WEB-S02 · Form values and result destinations

Correct answer: A — SIZE controls approximate visible text-input width.

WEB09 distinguishes size from maxlength: size describes the approximate visible width of a text input, while maxlength limits how much text can be entered. That matches the stem’s focus on characters displayed without scrolling. VALUE provides initial content and TYPE selects the control kind; neither is the width-setting attribute requested here.

Evidence in the complete study note

For a text input, size indicates approximate visible width, whereas maxlength limits entered text length.WEB09
For a text input, the value attribute supplies its initial text value; it does not specify the control’s width.WEB-S02

Choice by choice

A · correct — SIZE controls approximate visible width for a text input, matching the display-without-scrolling description.

B · incorrect — MAXLENGTH limits entered text length rather than determining how wide the input appears.

C · incorrect — VALUE supplies the control’s content, not its visible character-width setting.

D · incorrect — TYPE selects the input-control kind rather than its approximate visible width.

Question 4

Which statement is false about potential benefits of well-designed external style sheets? Treat benefits as possibilities, not guarantees.

  • A. Style sheets can support accessible presentation
  • B. Style sheets can create a consistent appearance
  • C. Style sheets can make HTML pages easier to maintain
  • D. Style sheets cannot reduce repeated markup or transferred file size

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 37

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

Study-guide sections

WEB11 · CSS attachment and selector meaning

WEB07 · Links, images and accessible meaning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB11 · CSS attachment and selector meaning

WEB07 · Links, images and accessible meaning

Correct answer: D — Style sheets cannot reduce repeated markup or transferred file size

External CSS lets several pages reuse presentation rules, making visual changes easier to maintain and helping consistency. Reuse and caching can reduce repeated markup and transfers, although savings depend on the implementation. Accessible presentation is also possible, but CSS alone does not establish accessibility. The false statement is the absolute denial of any size or transfer savings; the other choices describe potential benefits rather than universal promises.

Evidence in the complete study note

External CSS promotes reuse, consistent design and caching; it does not guarantee that every page becomes smaller or accessible.WEB11
Give controls programmatic labels, clear link text and keyboard access; visual styling alone does not establish accessibility.WEB07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Accessible presentation can be supported, though semantic markup and usable controls are still needed.

B · incorrect — Reused rules can give pages a consistent appearance.

C · incorrect — Central rules reduce repeated presentation edits across pages.

D · correct — This absolute denial is false: reuse and caching can reduce repeated markup and transfers.

Question 5

What will be the out of the following JavaScript statement? Math.abs(-9)

  • A. 9
  • B. -9
  • C. 1
  • D. 0

Source

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 62

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Track the value and type at each operation, applying the stated conversion, indexing or mathematical rule.

Study-guide sections

WEB-S08 · Numeric functions and NaN checks

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB-S08 · Numeric functions and NaN checks

Correct answer: A — 9

WEB18 explicitly evaluates Math.abs(-9) as 9. Absolute value removes the negative sign from a negative numeric argument and leaves its magnitude, so the result is neither the original negative number nor a Boolean-like one or zero. This is an expression result; no rounding or text conversion is involved.

Evidence in the complete study note

For finite numeric arguments, Math.abs(x) gives the nonnegative magnitude, Math.floor(x) gives the greatest integer no larger than x, and Math.sqrt(x) gives the nonnegative square root for nonnegative x.WEB-S08

Choice by choice

A · correct — The absolute value of negative nine is its nonnegative magnitude, nine.

B · incorrect — Negative nine is the input; absolute value does not preserve its negative sign.

C · incorrect — Math.abs returns numeric magnitude rather than a Boolean-like value of one.

D · incorrect — The input is nonzero, so its absolute value is not zero.

Question 6

In the legacy browser expression document.bgColor, what is bgColor?

  • A. bgColor is a method
  • B. bgColor is the document object
  • C. bgColor is a property
  • D. bgColor is an event handler

Adapted from

Study-guide sections

WEB22 · Window, dialogs and browser properties

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB22 · Window, dialogs and browser properties

Correct answer: C — bgColor is a property

The expression uses the lowercase document object name and the exact camelCase member bgColor. In this legacy API, bgColor is a property representing background color, rather than a method call or event handler. Asking specifically about the member avoids confusing it with window.document, which is itself a property. Current code normally changes the background through document.body.style.backgroundColor rather than this legacy interface.

document.bgColor is a legacy property; Document.bgcolor has wrong object/case.WEB22
In a normal browser page, window exposes the browsing context and document is its document property.WEB22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — No function is invoked or named by this legacy color member.

B · incorrect — document is the object on which the member is accessed, not the bgColor value.

C · correct — The legacy member stores a background-color setting.

D · incorrect — The member is a color property, not an event callback.

Question 7

Look at the following valid PHP array: $list = array("outside" => "red", "inside" => "brown", "top" => "black", "under" => "blue"); Which exact string key indexes the value "black"?

  • A. brown
  • B. outside
  • C. under
  • D. top

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 69

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

WEB26 · PHP arrays, loops and callable behavior

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB26 · PHP arrays, loops and callable behavior

Correct answer: D — top

PHP associative arrays map explicit keys to values. In each pair, the text before the contiguous => operator is the key and the text after it is the value. The pair containing black therefore uses the key top. String-key case matters, so the lowercase spelling is retained in the corrected choices. The other offered strings either identify another entry or are themselves a value rather than the requested key.

Evidence in the complete study note

PHP arrays map integer/string keys to values.WEB26
Associative syntax uses a contiguous => operator: ["top"=>"black"] stores black under key"top".WEB26

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — brown is the value associated with inside, not the key of black.

B · incorrect — outside identifies red.

C · incorrect — under identifies blue.

D · correct — top is the exact key paired with black.

Question 8

Which statement is false about modern JavaScript running in a browser sandbox?

  • A. The language cannot support sophisticated applications
  • B. Scripts can access selected client devices through permission-based APIs
  • C. Scripts have restricted access to arbitrary client files and hardware
  • D. Script source can be supplied as text and executed by the browser

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 75

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check exact language syntax, declaration rules and execution context before reasoning about the result.

Study-guide sections

WEB01 · Browser, server and technology roles

WEB15 · JavaScript syntax, inclusion and declarations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB01 · Browser, server and technology roles

WEB15 · JavaScript syntax, inclusion and declarations

Correct answer: A — The language cannot support sophisticated applications

Browser JavaScript supports sophisticated applications; its sandbox is a restriction on access to resources, not proof of an inherently weak language. Selected file or device access can be exposed through permission-based APIs, while arbitrary hardware access remains restricted. JavaScript source can be included in pages or loaded from a script file. Thus the language-capability claim is false, while the qualified environment and source-delivery claims are compatible.

Evidence in the complete study note

Browser scripts are sandboxed, but may access selected files/devices through permission-based APIs.WEB01
They are not inherently limited to trivial programs, nor can they freely access arbitrary client hardware.WEB01
Use <script src="app.js"></script> for an external .js file; script content has no HTML closing-tag syntax inside its JavaScript source.WEB15

Choice by choice

A · correct — The note explicitly allows sophisticated applications, so this denial is false.

B · incorrect — Permission-based APIs allow selected device access.

C · incorrect — Sandbox restrictions limit arbitrary resource access.

D · incorrect — Script inclusion supplies source for browser execution.

Question 44

A developer stores $_SESSION["user_id"] server-side and an editable logged_in cookie client-side. A protected endpoint grants access solely when logged_in=1 and never validates the server-side session. An unauthenticated attacker sets that cookie. Which statement is most accurate?

  • A. The endpoint is vulnerable: trusting the cookie alone bypasses the required server-session authorization
  • B. The endpoint is secure because server-side session data exists
  • C. The endpoint is vulnerable only if the genuine session ID is exposed
  • D. The endpoint is secure if HTTPS is used

WEB29 · Server sessions and the authorization trust path

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB29 · Server sessions and the authorization trust path

Correct answer: A — The endpoint is vulnerable: trusting the cookie alone bypasses the required server-session authorization

The protected endpoint trusts an attacker-controlled value rather than checking authenticated server-side state. Setting the flag is therefore sufficient to gain the access that should require session authorization. Merely storing a user ID elsewhere does not help when that state is never consulted. No genuine session identifier must be stolen for this bypass, and HTTPS protects transmission rather than proving that a client-generated authorization claim is true.

Evidence in the complete study note

A client cookie logged_in=1 is attacker-controlled.WEB29
If the server trusts it alone, authorization can be bypassed.WEB29
HTTPS does not make client-generated claims trustworthy.WEB29

Choice by choice

A · correct — The stated cookie-only authorization path allows the attacker to bypass the required session check.

B · incorrect — Unused server-side state does not protect this endpoint.

C · incorrect — No genuine session ID is needed when the endpoint trusts only the flag.

D · incorrect — Transport protection does not make a forged client flag trustworthy.

WEB19 · Control flow, functions and errors

Correct answer: B — the initialization, the test, and the update

The general form is for(initialization; test; update). Initialization runs once, the test decides whether another iteration starts, and the update follows each completed body. The first alternative also omits the test, so the aggregate alternative is incorrect.

D · incorrect — The first alternative omits the test, and the increment-only alternative is not the general form.

try/catch handles thrown errors during execution; throw signals one; finally runs cleanup.WEB19

D · incorrect — JavaScript does support exception handling through the mechanisms described in the complete note.

An appropriate inline event handler can use a false return value to cancel the handled event’s default action. Question 128

Which PHP mechanisms can participate in generating dynamic content and server-side processing? Select all that apply.

  • A. Functions
  • B. Variables
  • C. Classes
  • D. Objects

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 56

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

Study-guide sections

WEB26 · PHP arrays, loops and callable behavior

WEB33 · PHP includes, objects and dates

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB26 · PHP arrays, loops and callable behavior

WEB33 · PHP includes, objects and dates

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — Functions; Variables; Classes; Objects

Dynamic PHP responses can combine values, reusable behavior and object-based structures. Variables hold incoming or computed data; functions carry out processing; classes define application state and behavior; objects are instances used by that logic. None of these mechanisms alone defines dynamic PHP, but each can participate in it. The revised wording therefore asks for all contributors rather than forcing one exclusive mechanism from four compatible choices.

Evidence in the complete study note

A function can receive arguments, return a value, or produce output; classes/objects/variables also support server processing, so no single one of these mechanisms alone defines “dynamic PHP.” Use braces to make nesting explicit.WEB26
A class defines properties/methods; new creates an object, $obj->field accesses a property, and $obj->method() calls a method.WEB33

Choice by choice

A · correct — Functions can process inputs and return values or produce output.

B · correct — Variables hold request data and computed values used in a response.

C · correct — Classes define state and behavior for server application logic.

D · correct — Objects instantiate classes and can participate in generating responses.

Study-guide references

Correct answer: B — Sessions

In conventional server-backed sessions, the browser normally keeps an opaque identifier and the user’s session data resides in server-controlled storage. Cookies, localStorage and IndexedDB instead retain data on the client side. Client storage may participate in an application design, but it is not the server-side session-data store requested. Sessions therefore match the stated location.

IndexedDB supplies structured local storage.WEB28

B · correct — A server-backed session keeps the user’s session data in server-controlled storage.

C · incorrect — localStorage retains origin-specific strings in browser storage rather than storing the server’s session data.

D · incorrect — IndexedDB is structured local browser storage rather than the server’s session-data store.

  • A. 9
  • B. 11.8
  • C. 6
  • D. 5

Sources

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 24-2

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 81

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 27

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Track the value and type at each operation, applying the stated conversion, indexing or mathematical rule.

Study-guide sections

WEB-S08 · Numeric functions and NaN checks

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB-S08 · Numeric functions and NaN checks

Correct answer: D — 5

WEB18 directly evaluates Math.floor(5.9)=5. The floor operation gives the greatest integer not exceeding the input, rather than rounding to the nearest integer or multiplying the input. Thus the fractional part does not push the result up to six; the expression value is five. No string or DOM behavior changes this math result.

Evidence in the complete study note

For finite numeric arguments, Math.abs(x) gives the nonnegative magnitude, Math.floor(x) gives the greatest integer no larger than x, and Math.sqrt(x) gives the nonnegative square root for nonnegative x.WEB-S08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Nine is not the integer floor of 5.9; it is merely a digit appearing in the input.

B · incorrect — 11.8 doubles the input and is unrelated to the floor operation.

C · incorrect — Six would be upward or nearest-integer rounding here, not floor.

D · correct — Five is the greatest integer no larger than 5.9, matching the explicit note example.

Question 157

Which option identifies components present in an HTTP/1.1 request even when it has no message body?

  • A. Header fields only
  • B. Header fields and a mandatory body
  • C. A response status line, header fields and a mandatory body
  • D. A request line and header fields

Study-guide sections

WEB03 · Read an HTTP/1.1 exchange

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB03 · Read an HTTP/1.1 exchange

Correct answer: D — A request line and header fields

HTTP/1.1 requests start with a request line, then contain header fields and a terminating blank line. A body is optional, so neither option that requires one describes every request. A status line begins a response, not a request. The version qualifier matters because HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 encode messages differently; the selected components refer specifically to the textual HTTP/1.1 structure, not every HTTP wire format.

Evidence in the complete study note

An HTTP/1.1 request begins with method, request-target and version, followed by header fields, a blank line, and an optional body.WEB03
A response begins with version, status code and optional reason phrase, then headers, blank line and permitted content.WEB03

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — This omits the request line.

B · incorrect — The body is optional, so making it mandatory is wrong.

C · incorrect — A status line belongs to a response, and a request body is optional.

D · correct — These components are present before any optional body.

Question 158

What will be the output of the following code snippet? <script type="text/javascript" language= 'javascript' > var a = "exitexam"; var result = a.substring(2, 6); document.write(result); </script>

  • B. texam
  • C. itex
  • D. xite

WEB18 · Math, string and array API microtraces

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB18 · Math, string and array API microtraces

Correct answer: C — itex

substring(2,6) uses a zero-based start and excludes the end index. In exitexam, indices 2, 3, 4 and 5 contain i, t, e and x. document.write therefore emits itex. Starting at index 1 or continuing beyond index 5 produces a different interval, which rules out the other strings.

Evidence in the complete study note

A JS string’s substring(start,end) includes start and excludes end: "exitexam".substring(2,6) is "itex".WEB18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — xitex starts at index one and contains five characters, rather than the requested four-character interval.

B · incorrect — texam starts too late and extends beyond the exclusive end index six.

C · correct — Indices two through five contain i, t, e, x, producing itex.

D · incorrect — xite begins at index one rather than the specified zero-based start index two.

WEB25 states that a function’s locals and by-value parameters are separate bindings from variables outside it. Question 174

Study-guide sections

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Correct answer: C — Caching

WEB39 defines caching as reusing a representation or result and requiring validity or invalidation rules. Keeping frequently accessed data for reuse is therefore Caching. Compression and minification reduce transfer or source size, while encryption protects data; none of those alone stores a reusable computed result. Cache keys and privacy still matter when using the technique safely.

D · incorrect — Encryption protects data confidentiality rather than supplying the result-reuse technique described.

WEB-S14 · Application protocols and underlying communication

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB05 · HTTPS and resource-oriented APIs

WEB-S14 · Application protocols and underlying communication

Correct answer: D — HTTPS

WEB05 defines HTTPS as HTTP over TLS, protecting channel confidentiality and integrity and authenticating the server through certificate checks. That is the secure web-communication protocol among the main choices. Plain HTTP, FTP, and TCP/IP do not by their names supply that TLS-protected web exchange. The alternate option set places HTTPS at C, so its answer letter differs.

Evidence in the complete study note

HTTPS uses HTTP over TLS, protecting channel confidentiality/integrity and authenticating the server under certificate checks.WEB05
HTTP defines web application requests, response status codes and representations.WEB-S14
An HTTP exchange can use underlying TCP connections and IP addresses; naming that network stack does not identify the application-level method or status semantics.WEB-S14
FTP is a file-transfer application protocol.WEB-S14
SMTP transports electronic mail.WEB-S14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Plain HTTP does not by itself add TLS confidentiality, integrity, and certificate-based server authentication.

B · incorrect — FTP is not the HTTPS protocol for TLS-protected web communication identified in the note.

C · incorrect — TCP/IP names underlying networking protocols rather than the TLS-protected HTTP scheme requested.

D · correct — HTTPS is HTTP over TLS and supplies the channel protections described in WEB05.

Alternative version 1

Correct answer: C — HTTPS

This variant moves HTTPS to C and replaces the fourth choice with SMTP. WEB05 still identifies HTTPS as HTTP over TLS. HTTP alone lacks that channel protection, and FTP or SMTP does not name the secure web protocol requested, so the variant answer must use its own C label.

HTTPS uses HTTP over TLS, protecting channel confidentiality/integrity and authenticating the server under certificate checks.WEB05

HTTP defines web application requests, response status codes and representations.WEB-S14

An HTTP exchange can use underlying TCP connections and IP addresses; naming that network stack does not identify the application-level method or status semantics.WEB-S14

FTP is a file-transfer application protocol.WEB-S14

SMTP transports electronic mail.WEB-S14

A · incorrect — Plain HTTP does not itself provide the TLS channel protections described in WEB05.

B · incorrect — FTP is not the TLS-protected HTTP protocol used for the requested secure web exchange.

C · correct — HTTPS is HTTP over TLS, protecting confidentiality, integrity, and checked server identity.

D · incorrect — SMTP is not the HTTPS web protocol and does not answer the secure HTTP communication question.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB28 · Cookies and browser storage

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — Cookies; Local storage; Session storage; IndexedDB

All four entries are browser storage techniques, although their persistence, data model and automatic transmission behavior differ. Cookies hold browser name/value data that can accompany matching requests. localStorage persists origin-specific strings, sessionStorage is scoped to a page session or tab, and IndexedDB supports structured local data. The revised question asks for every local-storage technique rather than assuming that only the API named local storage qualifies.

Evidence in the complete study note

IndexedDB supplies structured local storage.WEB28

Choice by choice

A · correct — Cookies are browser-held name/value data, even though matching requests can transmit them.

B · correct — localStorage persists origin-specific string values until removed or cleared.

C · correct — sessionStorage stores browser data within a page-session or tab scope.

D · correct — IndexedDB supplies structured local browser storage.

Question 193

Which source-processing step removes unnecessary characters from CSS or JavaScript, distinct from bundling files together or compressing transfer encoding?

  • B. Caching
  • C. Minification
  • D. Encryption

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 83

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Correct answer: C — Minification

Minification removes unnecessary source characters, such as dispensable formatting, while preserving the intended program or stylesheet behavior. Bundling combines files and compression changes transfer encoding; these are separate operations even when a build pipeline performs them together. Caching instead reuses an existing representation, and encryption serves confidentiality. Restricting the question to source-character reduction makes minification the supported technique without claiming it also performs file combination.

Evidence in the complete study note

Minification removes unnecessary source characters; bundling combines files; compression changes transfer encoding; preloading fetches anticipated resources early.WEB39
Caching reuses a representation/result and requires validity/invalidation rules.WEB39

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Compression changes transfer encoding rather than performing the specified source-character reduction.

B · incorrect — Caching reuses a representation rather than rewriting its source characters.

C · correct — Minification is the source-character reduction step.

D · incorrect — Encryption protects confidentiality rather than simplifying source formatting.

Question 199

Which client-side technique is used to optimize web page loading speed by preloading resources in advance?

  • B. Minification
  • C. Caching
  • D. Preloading

Source

Study-guide sections

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB39 · Manage content, performance and revisions

Correct answer: D — Preloading

WEB39 defines preloading as fetching anticipated resources early. That exactly matches preloading resources in advance in the stem. Compression and minification change transfer or source size, while caching reuses a representation already obtained. Preloading can help loading speed when chosen well, but excessive early fetching can compete with critical work, so performance should be measured.

Minification removes unnecessary source characters; bundling combines files; compression changes transfer encoding; preloading fetches anticipated resources early.WEB39

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — Minification removes unnecessary source characters rather than prefetching resources before demand.

C · incorrect — Caching reuses retained results; it is distinct from initiating an early fetch of anticipated resources.

D · correct — Preloading fetches anticipated resources early, matching the advance-loading technique described.

Question 227

Which situations demonstrate concurrency when their requests make overlapping progress? Here simultaneously means overlapping progress, not necessarily execution at the same instant. Select all that apply.

  • A. The ability of the server to handle multiple clients simultaneously
  • B. The ability of the client to handle multiple servers simultaneously
  • C. The ability of the server to handle multiple requests from a single client
  • D. The ability of the client to handle multiple requests to a single server

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — The ability of the server to handle multiple clients simultaneously; The ability of the client to handle multiple servers simultaneously; The ability of the server to handle multiple requests from a single client; The ability of the client to handle multiple requests to a single server

Concurrency means overlapping progress, whereas parallelism requires execution at the same instant. A server can overlap work for several clients or several requests from one client. A client can likewise overlap interactions with several servers or multiple requests to one server. The question explicitly supplies overlap for each situation, making every listed arrangement an example of concurrency without asserting that all work physically runs in parallel.

Question 228

What is a race condition in the context of concurrency?

  • A. A condition where two or more clients compete to establish a connection with the server
  • B. A condition where two or more servers compete to respond to a client request
  • C. A condition where multiple threads or processes access shared resources in an unpredictable manner
  • D. A condition where multiple clients send duplicate requests to the server

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 118

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the shared-state invariant and the operations that must be coordinated.

Study-guide sections

WEB37 · Races, locks and transaction invariants

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB37 · Races, locks and transaction invariants

Correct answer: C — Shared-resource correctness depends on execution interleaving.

WEB37 describes two requests reading stock one, both accepting a sale, and both writing zero. The final correctness depends on their interleaving, which is the race-condition mechanism captured most closely by C’s unpredictable shared-resource access. Competing connections, multiple responders, or duplicate requests are not themselves sufficient; they become races only when shared-state correctness depends on timing.

Evidence in the complete study note

Suppose two requests read a stock count1, both decide it is available and both write0: two sales consumed one item.WEB37
Correctness depends on interleaving, even if each callback has only a short synchronous body.WEB37

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Competition to establish a connection is not by itself a shared-state correctness failure caused by interleaving.

B · incorrect — Several servers responding does not alone establish a race on shared mutable state.

C · correct — This is the closest option: shared-state access can make correctness depend on the execution interleaving.

D · incorrect — Duplicate requests can cause other problems, but duplication alone is not the defining race-condition mechanism.

Question 229

Which technique directly protects one shared-state critical section with an exclusive lock that does not rely on busy waiting? Choose the exclusive-lock primitive, rather than a bounded-access counter or a messaging design.

  • A. Mutex locks
  • B. Spinlocks
  • C. Semaphores
  • D. Message queues

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 119

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the shared-state invariant and the operations that must be coordinated.

Study-guide sections

WEB37 · Races, locks and transaction invariants

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB37 · Races, locks and transaction invariants

Correct answer: A — Mutex locks

A mutex directly protects a critical section by allowing only one holder at a time. The question distinguishes that exclusive-lock abstraction from spinlock busy waiting, semaphore bounded-access counting and message-queue designs. A semaphore can also enforce exclusion when configured suitably, but it is not the specific exclusive-lock primitive requested. Choosing a primitive does not by itself guarantee application correctness: every conflicting update must use the protected critical section.

Evidence in the complete study note

A mutex protects one critical section; semaphores can coordinate bounded access; spinlocks busy-wait and are unsuitable for blocking a browser/event-loop thread.WEB37

Choice by choice

A · correct — A mutex is the requested exclusive-lock primitive.

B · incorrect — A spinlock relies on busy waiting, which the stem excludes.

C · incorrect — A semaphore is the bounded-access counter abstraction excluded by the requested category.

D · incorrect — A message queue is a messaging design rather than the requested lock primitive.

  • C. A function that is called by the server to handle concurrent client requests
  • D. A function that is called by the client to synchronize with the server

Study-guide references

WEB34 · AJAX and response handling

Correct answer: A — A function invoked by the browser runtime or API when the response becomes available

The callback is registered for later invocation by the browser runtime or API when the response becomes available. The remote server sends response data; it does not directly execute the browser function. A function that starts a request or a server request-handler function has a different role in the described interaction. The answer states both the owning execution environment and the event that causes invocation.

A callback is a function invoked later by the runtime/API.WEB34

B · incorrect — Starting a request is not the response callback’s role.

C · incorrect — A server request handler is a different callback in a different environment.

D · incorrect — A callback need not perform client/server synchronization.

Question 231

Which application-level protocol provides a persistent bidirectional message channel after its handshake?

  • A. HTTP
  • B. FTP
  • C. TCP/IP
  • D. WebSocket

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 121

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the execution side and communication pattern, keeping runtime, transport, data format and callback roles distinct.

WEB35 · Polling, WebSockets and data formats

WEB-S14 · Application protocols and underlying communication

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB35 · Polling, WebSockets and data formats

WEB-S14 · Application protocols and underlying communication

Correct answer: D — WebSocket

WebSocket establishes a persistent bidirectional channel on which either endpoint can exchange messages after the handshake. HTTP requests can also be issued asynchronously, but asynchronous programming alone does not supply this specific channel model. FTP has a different transfer role, and TCP/IP names lower-level networking foundations rather than the requested application protocol. The revised interaction requirement therefore distinguishes WebSocket without claiming it is the only way to avoid blocking a client.

Evidence in the complete study note

WebSocket establishes a persistent bidirectional message channel after its handshake.WEB35
Either HTTP-based AJAX or WebSockets can support nonblocking user interaction and carry JSON, so generic questions may be nonexclusive.WEB35
HTTP defines web application requests, response status codes and representations.WEB-S14
An HTTP exchange can use underlying TCP connections and IP addresses; naming that network stack does not identify the application-level method or status semantics.WEB-S14
FTP is a file-transfer application protocol.WEB-S14
SMTP transports electronic mail.WEB-S14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Asynchronous HTTP requests do not by themselves define this persistent bidirectional message channel.

B · incorrect — FTP is not the specified WebSocket-style application messaging protocol.

C · incorrect — TCP/IP refers to lower-level networking rather than this application-level channel protocol.

D · correct — WebSocket supplies the described persistent bidirectional channel.

Question 232

What is long polling in client-server communication?

  • A. A technique where the server continuously sends updates to the client
  • B. A technique where the client continuously sends requests to the server for updates

Identify the execution side and communication pattern, keeping runtime, transport, data format and callback roles distinct.

WEB35 · Polling, WebSockets and data formats

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB35 · Polling, WebSockets and data formats

Correct answer: C — The server holds a client request until data is available or timeout occurs.

WEB35 defines long polling as holding a client request until an event or timeout, returning a response, and then reconnecting from the client. C captures that defining held-request step. It is not continuous unsolicited streaming on a finished response, repeated short polling without a held request, or a reversed arrangement in which a client holds a server-originated request.

Evidence in the complete study note

Short polling repeatedly requests updates.WEB35
Long polling holds one client request until an event or timeout, returns a response, then the client reconnects; it is not continuous unsolicited streaming on that same finished response.WEB35

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Continuous unsolicited server updates describe streaming-like behavior rather than the held-request long-polling cycle.

B · incorrect — Repeated immediate polling requests describe short polling rather than holding each request until an event or timeout.

C · correct — Holding the client’s request until new data or timeout is the defining long-polling behavior.

D · incorrect — This reverses the roles; the server holds a request initiated by the client.

Question 249

A web application has two protected endpoints. The profile endpoint checks a valid session identifier and its server-side user record on every request. The transfer endpoint grants access whenever the editable logged_in cookie equals 1 and ignores session validation. An unauthenticated attacker has no valid session and sets logged_in=1. Which result follows from these access checks?

  • A. The cookie edit can bypass the transfer endpoint, but does not grant access to the profile endpoint
  • B. The cookie edit grants access to both endpoints because both receive the same cookie
  • C. Neither endpoint can be bypassed unless the attacker first obtains a genuine session identifier
  • D. HTTPS alone prevents either endpoint from accepting a forged logged_in value

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 93

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Follow the identifier and server-side state through the stated lifecycle or access check; distinguish client-controlled claims from server decisions.

Study-guide sections

WEB29 · Server sessions and the authorization trust path

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

WEB29 · Server sessions and the authorization trust path

Correct answer: A — The cookie edit can bypass the transfer endpoint, but does not grant access to the profile endpoint

The two endpoints use different trust paths. The transfer endpoint trusts an attacker-controlled flag, so the forged value satisfies its stated access check without a valid session. The profile endpoint requires authenticated server-side state, which the attacker lacks, so the unrelated cookie does not grant access there. HTTPS protects transport rather than validating the truth of a client-generated login claim. The bypass therefore affects the transfer endpoint only.

Evidence in the complete study note

A client cookie logged_in=1 is attacker-controlled.WEB29
If the server trusts it alone, authorization can be bypassed.WEB29
If the server checks a valid session ID and its server-side user/role on every protected action, editing that unrelated flag does not grant rights.WEB29
HTTPS does not make client-generated claims trustworthy.WEB29

Choice by choice

A · correct — Only the transfer endpoint relies solely on the forgeable flag; the profile endpoint still requires a valid session.

B · incorrect — Receiving the same cookie does not make the endpoints apply the same authorization rule.

C · incorrect — The transfer check requires no genuine session identifier, so stealing one is unnecessary for that bypass.

D · incorrect — HTTPS does not prevent a client from submitting a false authorization flag.

Study-guide references

WEB09 · Form controls and successful submission

WEB07 · Links, images and accessible meaning

Correct answer: D — Provide an accessible label associated with the input.

WEB09 links a label’s for to the control id, and WEB07 requires programmatic control labels. That association lets assistive technology identify the input and announce its label. It does not alter storage, encryption, or network submission speed. D states the accessibility purpose directly, rather than confusing it with unrelated browser or transport features.

Question 251

What is the difference between GET and POST methods? When would you use each?

    Answer & Detailed Explanation

    Study-guide references

    WEB04 · Methods, status and GET/POST reasoning

    WEB40 · Assemble and evaluate an end-to-end feature

    Answer: GET retrieves safely and usually places form values in the query; POST asks the target to process body content.

    WEB04 recommends GET for reading representations rather than intentional state changes. POST suits submitted processing or actions such as enrollment with proper authorization and CSRF controls. Neither method encrypts data; use HTTPS for channel protection. POST body values remain visible to tools and subject to configured size limits rather than becoming secret or unlimited.

    POST asks the target to process supplied content.WEB04
    GET forms usually put name/value pairs in the URL query; POST forms put them in the body.WEB04
    For an enrollment action use POST with CSRF controls, server authorization, capacity checks and a transaction; show success only after commit.WEB40

    Question 252

    Why is client-side validation alone not enough for security?

      WEB27 · Request data, server validation and injection

      WEB21 · Events and validated submission

      Answer: Clients can bypass or alter browser checks, so the server must validate and authorize again.

      WEB27 requires server checks for required fields, type, length, and range, plus authentication and authorization before processing.       Bind SQL parameters to keep values separate from commands.WEB27

      Question 253

        WEB20 · DOM selection, creation and safe updates

        Answer & Detailed Explanation

        Study-guide references

        WEB20 · DOM selection, creation and safe updates

        Answer: The DOM is the document’s node hierarchy, enabling scripts to inspect and update page content and behavior.

        WEB20 selects nodes, creates elements, and attaches them to that hierarchy. Creating a node does not itself insert it, and missing lookups must be guarded. textContent safely inserts untrusted plain text, whereas innerHTML reparses markup and can replace descendant state.         Creation alone does not insert it.WEB20

          Answer: A persistent remember/session token or browser restoration can preserve the login flow.

          Question 255

          Why would a developer choose local storage over cookies?

            Source

            • Web Programming review questions · Question 5

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

            Study-guide sections

            WEB28 · Cookies and browser storage

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB28 · Cookies and browser storage

            Answer: localStorage persists origin data without automatically attaching it to every matching request.

            WEB28 contrasts localStorage’s persistent strings with cookies’ automatic request transmission. It can avoid transmitting data needed only by the client. JavaScript can still send stored tokens explicitly, so localStorage is not inherently incapable of session designs. Script-access risks and persistence policies must be considered; neither mechanism is universally preferable for sensitive authentication data.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            localStorage persists origin-specific string values across sessions until removed/cleared; sessionStorage is scoped to a page session/tab.WEB28
            Neither is automatically transmitted like matching cookies, but JavaScript can send stored data explicitly.WEB28
            Thus all four are client storage techniques, and localStorage can participate in token-based session designs, with script-access risks.WEB28

            WEB32 · SQL operations, result rows and safe rendering

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB32 · SQL operations, result rows and safe rendering

            Correct answer: B — mysqli_insert_id($conn), for a generated AUTO_INCREMENT value on that connection.

            WEB32 identifies mysqli_insert_id($conn) as reporting the connection’s generated AUTO_INCREMENT value. It is not a universal lookup of an arbitrary last row or a promise of gapless IDs. B names the correct function; the others invent different names. A connection argument and appropriate successful insertion context are needed in actual procedural code.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            mysqli_num_rows counts a result’s rows; mysqli_affected_rows($conn) counts changed/inserted/deleted rows under its options; mysqli_insert_id($conn) reports a generated AUTO_INCREMENT value from the connection.WEB32
            AUTO_INCREMENT generates numeric values but gaps and explicit values are possible; do not promise gapless consecutive business numbering.WEB32

            A · incorrect — mysqli_last_id() is not the generated-value function named in WEB32.

            B · correct — mysqli_insert_id($conn) reports the connection’s generated AUTO_INCREMENT value.

            C · incorrect — mysqli_get_id() is not the API identified for the generated insert value.

            D · incorrect — mysqli_row_id() is not the API named for a generated insert identifier.

            Question 292

            Which ordinary PHP variable scope can be accessed inside a function using a global declaration or, alternatively, the $GLOBALS array?

            • A. Local
            • B. Static
            • C. Global
            • D. Session

            Adapted from

            • Web Programming review questions · Question 37

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

            Study-guide sections

            WEB25 · PHP scope, parameters and persistent locals

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB25 · PHP scope, parameters and persistent locals

            Correct answer: C — Global

            A variable declared outside functions has global scope. A function normally has separate local bindings, so it can explicitly import such a binding with global or access it through $GLOBALS. The keyword is therefore one mechanism, not a mandatory exclusive spelling. A static local remains a function-local binding whose value persists across calls; session state belongs to a superglobal available across scopes.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A variable outside a function has global scope.WEB25
            A function’s locals and by-value parameters are separate bindings; use global $x or $GLOBALS["x"] to refer to a global explicitly.WEB25
            A static local retains its value across calls during the execution lifecycle; static storage is not simply another visibility scope.WEB25
            Superglobals are available across scopes.WEB25

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Ordinary local bindings already belong to that function; this is not importing an outside binding.

            B · incorrect — A static local retains its value across calls but remains local to the function.

            C · correct — Global bindings are the outside-function bindings accessed by these two mechanisms.

            D · incorrect — Session state uses a superglobal available across scopes, rather than this ordinary binding import.

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB25 · PHP scope, parameters and persistent locals

            WEB23 · PHP syntax, names and types

            Correct answer: C — A local variable that retains its value between calls during the execution lifecycle.

            WEB25 defines a static local by persistence across function calls. It remains a local binding and can change value; static is not the same as constant, global visibility, or server session storage. Thus C supplies both the local-scope and retained-state aspects, without treating static duration as an independent universal visibility scope.

            B · incorrect — Static persistence does not make the variable a global visible everywhere.

            C · correct — A static local retains its value across calls during the execution lifecycle.

            Question 296

            For ordinary HTML form submission, which statement correctly contrasts where POST places form data with GET’s URL query?

            • A. POST is faster than GET
            • B. POST data is visible in the URL
            • C. POST form data normally goes in the request body rather than the URL query, subject to configured size limits
            • D. POST is easier to implement

            Adapted from

            • Web Programming review questions · Question 41

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify the protocol layer and the intended request, response or channel semantics.

            Study-guide sections

            WEB04 · Methods, status and GET/POST reasoning

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB04 · Methods, status and GET/POST reasoning

            Correct answer: C — POST form data normally goes in the request body rather than the URL query, subject to configured size limits

            Ordinary GET forms place name/value pairs in the URL query, whereas POST forms place them in the request body. This is a placement distinction, not encryption: tools can inspect the body, and servers impose configured limits. The other claims either put POST fields in the wrong location or assert universal speed/ease advantages that do not follow from the method semantics.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            GET forms usually put name/value pairs in the URL query; POST forms put them in the body.WEB04
            Neither method encrypts data.WEB04
            POST bodies are visible to developer tools and subject to server/configured size limits.WEB04

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Method choice does not guarantee that a POST operation is faster; this is not the placement contrast asked for.

            B · incorrect — Ordinary POST form values are placed in the body, not the URL query used by GET forms.

            C · correct — This gives the body-versus-query distinction while retaining configured limits and making no secrecy claim.

            D · incorrect — Ease of implementation is application-dependent and does not describe the form-data placement difference.

            Question 300

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            WEB30 · Uploads, files and storage safety

            Correct answer: B — Hints which file types the browser’s file picker should offer

            accept is a browser selection hint describing file types the picker should offer. It does not guarantee what an attacker can submit or what the server actually accepts. Server-side validation must separately check upload errors, size and content before safe storage. The attribute also neither initiates transfer, sets a maximum upload size nor validates a filename. The choice states the UI role without claiming server enforcement.
